[V-fetched] by one refuter from arxiv.org/html/2410.05565: "we remove the diagonal part of the adjacency matrix in the inverse" (READ docs/sources/design/refute_falsify_math.md §3.15); the sub-stochastic reading RUN[J] row sums \(0.400\dots0.765\) against \(1.000\) diagonal-kept (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §2.0); the extractor hazard the record paid for once — pypdf mapped \(-\) to \x00 and \(\infty\) to the glyph 1, turning an open interval into a closed one (READ workdonenewseal.md:468-473; V15_X36_PRIOR_ART.md:45-56 @ 99777ab); the bibliography verified at the identifier not the equation: \(278/278\) arXiv, \(91/92\) DOI (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §8). No LaTeX source has been read: NOT MEASURED — needs one fetch of the arXiv source, an author action outside this canon's no-fetch rule. Mechanism. P-10, V-24, V-3 (the identity half is against the lane's own re-implementation), P-6, FOUND-not-NAMED (neither arm exists; the kill's earlier reason presumed both did), V-15 (a plant that needs an arm that does not exist is itself NAMED), P-4. Kill. The LaTeX source contradicts the HTML reading (ChaCAL keeps the diagonal): the labels swap on the manifest, and every table row naming "ChaCAL-published" is re-labelled in a corrections row; price \(0\) GPU-s, no cell re-run. The reason the relabelling costs nothing is restated, because the earlier reason was false. It is not that both arms are FOUND: neither is, and a relabelling would touch cells that do not exist — RUN this session, grep -rniE 'chacal|infsa' --include='*.py' . (excluding .venv) returns \(0\) lines, and the \(24\)-kind census over results/**/*.jsonl holds \(0\) records for chacal_diag and \(0\) for chacal_published (04.11, 04.14). The relabelling is free because the convention question is decided before either arm exists, so there is nothing to relabel: the decision fixes which arithmetic a future make_arm branch emits under which name, and it is taken at specification time, at \(0\) GPU-s, with no journal touched. Both arms are marked NOT MEASURED — needs the ChaCAL control implementations (one make_arm branch, one optimizer path and one field emit per control, $41$–$130$ GPU-s per branch on 04.14'sarm_plbasis), and no sentence of this verse compares them on any bed. Planted negative — priced with no arm at all. The earlier plant ("the two arms must differ by \(O(1)\) at \(\gamma=0.9\) on the same \(P\)") required two arms that do not exist and was therefore itself NAMED, which 04.13's own Kill strikes ("any plant that exists only in a script's print (NAMED)"). It is replaced by a pure arithmetic assertion on a pinned random causal softmax \(A\), checkable at \(0\) GPU-s with no arm, no make_arm branch and no journal: on every row \(i\), \((A\mathbb 1)_i=1\) and \((A_s\mathbb 1)_i=1-A_{ii}<1\) strictly, the strictness carried by \(A_{ii}>0\) for a causal softmax (the bed's own diagonal read is \(\max_i\hat P_{ii}=0.692660\), 04.2), and the printed gap is \(\min_i A_{ii}\). The must-fire half: an \(A\) built with its diagonal logit at \(-\infty\) makes \(A_s=A\), the gap reads \(0\) exactly, and the check must report the two conventions indistinguishable — the known-degenerate case the assertion fires on. If the assertion cannot be evaluated on a pinned instance, the convention field is not wired and the kill cannot see it. If killed — link 1: the question asked of the operator, with no arm and no label. If the LaTeX read swaps the labels, the canon does not chase the naming; it asks whether the distinction the names carry is non-empty on this book's own bed, on an object no arm touches. The link's decisiveness rests on the discriminator reading $0$, and **falls the moment it does not**: a single record carryingboundary_setsmakes the recompute a hash move on a published cell and routes to link 2. **If killed — link 2: the field list is frozen instead of the cells.** If a shape-lane cell does exist, no hash is recomputed at all; instead the **field list itself** is hashed intoinstrument_hash, so a later addition or removal of a field is visible without touching any cell'smanifest_hash, and a cell whose field set does not match itsinstrument_hash's list is refused at the journal. This is a **different object** (the field list, not a cell), a **different instrument** (a hash over a static specification, not a re-emission of any record) and a **different number** (a mismatch count between two field sets, not a moved cell hash), so it does not die with link 1. *Hypotheses:*instrument_hashis already a declared field of this verse and is emitted per cell; the field list is fixed at birth and changes only throughCORRECTIONS.md. *Evidence:*instrument_hash, manifest_hashare in the field list above; L-2's precedent, $0$ of $24$ banked cells attributable because no cell journalled the four scalars (READV20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md:23 @ 99777ab); the count of distinctinstrument_hashvalues underresults/isNOT MEASURED — needs one grep once any shape-lane cell exists. *Kill:* two cells sharing oneinstrument_hashand carrying different field sets — the freeze does not bind and the lane has no identity at the specification level either; decided by one grep at $0$ GPU-s, and **more decisive** than link 1 because it settles the specification for every future cell rather than one cell's hash. **Terminal.** "No cell in the shape lane exists without its boundary condition, route and certificate inputs in its hash — and today no cell in the shape lane exists at all:kindarm_ceqreads $0$ records andboundary_setsreads $0$ records across all ofresults/. The $425$arm_smprime` records are another lane and are not evidence for or against anything in this book."

docs.title: 04.16 — The F0–F4 grading rubric, written out, and the gate that reads every cell (B18)
docs.text:
Statement. The rubric the record cited and never wrote, stated as decision rules: | token | decision rule | what it is not | |---|---|---| | F0 | the claim is exact with no tolerance and is carried by a machine-checked declaration that builds with the three-axiom set | a float instance alone | | F1 | a bound holds on the graded object with its constant printed in the object's units | a mask-sense F1 (L-CERT's \(\delta\)), a different object | | F2 | a direction or ordering holds and no constant is stated | a failed F1 | | F3 | the claim is a fact about the harness, not the theory (a flag missing, a timer unsynchronised) | a failed instance | | F4-D | the theory's domain is empty on the graded bed (a census admits \(0\) per cent) | — | | F4-W | the claim was withdrawn by its author | — | | F4-U | the claim was never attempted | — | The three F4 senses carry three tokens because one token cannot be read. The gate reads every cell, including every F4 cell, and grades a cell once, in one file, with any later grade a supersedes row (L-G2). TERMINAL means no further theorem can change the grade (a domain gap, a harness fact, a withdrawn claim); NOT-PUT means never graded; the two are distinct tokens and a cell carries at most one. The rubric's own date is 2026-09-05, and the suffix requirement binds from that date forward only. Before it the three F4 senses had one token, so every pre-rubric cell carries a bare F4 by construction and a suffix requirement applied retroactively would be satisfied at registration and then exempted by the grandfather clause in the same verse — a rule that fires \(68\) times and is waived \(68\) times decides nothing (V-3, V-10). The exact count is printed: RUN this session, git show 99777ab:V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md | grep -oE 'F4-?[DWU]?' reads \(31\) bare F4 and \(0\) suffixed, and the same over V20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md reads \(37\) bare and \(0\) suffixed — \(68\) bare tokens, \(0\) suffixed, across the two files. The one-off migration is therefore scheduled, not grandfathered: all \(68\) pre-rubric bare F4 tokens are re-graded into F4-D / F4-W / F4-U by reading each cell's own reason, each re-grade filed as a new row with a supersedes pointer to the bare one and neither row edited (L-G2), priced at \(0\) GPU-s and \(1\) evening as a row of 05 REPAIRS. Until that migration lands the two files hold \(68\) bare tokens and this book prints the count rather than treating them as graded. Hypotheses. A grade is a property of (cell, bed, date); the rubric's date is 2026-09-05 and the suffix clause of the Kill is asserted only of cells graded on or after it; a cell graded under an older rubric keeps its token with the rubric's date beside it and appears in the migration count above, so the exemption is a scheduled debt with a printed size, never a silent waiver. Evidence. L-GRADE (F0–F4 + HOW-BAD gap) cited once at READ CEQ_V20_R15_CONTRACT.md:58 @ 99777ab and no rubric text in the tree; JUPITER's reconstruction ruled BOUND to its usage, SATURN's ruled NOT BOUND on eight counterexamples (READ V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md:20-58 @ 99777ab); the five counterexamples there: F4 overloaded three ways; F2 and F3 not ordered; M14 carrying three grades in three files, resolved F4 at it.17; an F4 row reporting a live constant \(1.421901019003236\); two contradictory grades for one object filed by one office. The gate graded seven distinct failures on eight cells and could not see Q2/W1, Q6/W1, Q6/W3 (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §4.4). Mechanism. P-11, P-3, V-14a, M-20, L-G2, V-3 (a rule waived exactly as often as it fires), V-10 (a gate satisfied at registration). Kill. A cell carrying two different live grades in two files — whatever their dates — where a grade is live iff no row carrying a supersedes pointer to it exists; a cell the gate's population omits; an F4 without its suffix on a cell graded on or after 2026-09-05 — the restriction is the kill's, not an exemption granted after it fires, and the \(68\) pre-rubric bare tokens are carried by the migration line above rather than by a waiver. "At the same date" is struck from the first clause and the reason is printed, because it made the clause's own planted negative unable to satisfy it: the M14 triple spans it.3, it.17 and the contract, so a same-date requirement excluded the one known-bad case the clause exists to catch (V-15). A cell with two live grades is a defect whatever their dates — L-G2's whole device is that a superseded grade keeps a supersede marker, so the marker, and not the date, is what separates a superseded reading from a live contradiction. Instrument, pinned like every READ in this book, because both graded files were deleted from the working tree on 2026-09-05 (RUN this session, ls V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md V20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md reads No such file or directory for both, and both are readable only at the pin): 

git show 99777ab:V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md | grep -oE 'F4-?[DWU]?' | sort | uniq -c
git show 99777ab:V20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md  | grep -oE 'F4-?[DWU]?' | sort | uniq -c
git show 99777ab:V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md | grep -nE 'F4([^-]|$)'
git show 99777ab:V20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md  | grep -nE 'F4([^-]|$)'
The first two are the token census (RUN this session: \(31\) bare F4 and \(0\) suffixed in the theory table, \(37\) and \(0\) in the ledger); the last two locate the rows (\(28\) matching lines in each file, RUN this session) and are what the date filter and the supersedes read run over. A lookahead form (grep -nE 'F4(?![-])') is not POSIX ERE and does not run under grep -E; F4([^-]|$) is the form that does, and it is printed so the instrument is executable rather than described. The supersedes marker exists in both files at the pin (RUN this session, grep -cin 'supersed' reads \(1\) line in the theory table and \(7\) in the ledger), so the live/superseded distinction is readable there today. Price \(0\) GPU-s. Planted negative, now satisfying the kill's own condition: the M14 triple (F3 in the contract, F4 in the ledger, F1 in the journal) carries two live grades on one cell — the it.3 F1 was left on the far side of the it.4 freeze with no supersedes pointer written to it when it.17 ruled M14 = F4 (READ V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md:48-50 @ 99777ab) — so under the date-free clause the check must report M14 as one cell with two live grades and the kill fires on the known-bad case; under the struck "at the same date" wording it could not, because it.3 and it.17 are different dates. The must-not-fire half: a cell whose earlier grade does carry a supersedes pointer to it must not be reported, which is the two-way calibration the live/superseded reading needs. And a post-rubric row written with a bare F4 must be caught by the date-filtered grep, where the same token in a pre-rubric row must not be, which is the two-way calibration the date restriction needs. If killed — link 1. The later-dated grade stands with a supersedes pointer to the earlier; both remain in the file. Hypotheses: every grade row carries a date and a file (04.16's own statement). Evidence: the M14 resolution at it.17 (M14 = F4, RULING J-17d) left the it.3 F1 on the far side of the it.4 freeze with no supersedes pointer written to it, which is exactly the live pair the repaired Kill fires on and exactly what this link repairs (READ V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md:48-50 @ 99777ab, readable only at the pin — RUN this session, ls V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md reads No such file or directory). Kill: an edit of the earlier row — L-G2 violated, the table is struck; decided by a diff of the file against its previous commit, price \(0\) GPU-s. Terminal. "Every cell graded on or after 2026-09-05 carries one token from the seven above, one date and one file, and exactly one live grade across every file whatever the dates, a superseded grade being one a supersedes row points at; the gate's population equals the table's population; and \(68\) pre-rubric bare F4 tokens — \(31\) in V20_R15_THEORY_TABLE.md and \(37\) in V20_R15_LEAP_LEDGER.md at 99777ab, \(0\) suffixed — stand un-migrated with their count printed until 05 REPAIRS files their supersedes rows."

docs.title: 04.17 — The calibration column and its scoring rule
docs.text: Statement. One append-only column across rounds: bet id, source \(\in\{\)author, leap\(\}\), prediction, counter of equal specificity, deciding number, frozen PASS, frozen KILL, realised value, verdict \(\in\{\)HOLDS, COUNTER, SPLIT, VOID\(\}\), sign of the miss (\(+\) credits the project more than the measurement supports; \(-\) understates; unsigned for a contradiction), date, producer command. Rule: a VOID row (bed not admitted, or an instrument failing its plants) is unscored, never a miss; a SPLIT row is scored wrong with the sign of the optimistic half; the one-sided sign test runs on the pooled column after \(\ge8\) scored rows and on the two sources separately; a column at or above \(0.75\) optimistic after eight rows makes the counter the reported estimate for every unscored bet; the denominator is fixed before the audit and confirmations are listed beside findings. Hypotheses. Every prediction ships its counter before the data (D-7); the column is never edited, only appended (D-CALIB-5). Evidence. R11: \(9\) checked, \(9\) adverse, \(7\) +, \(1\) −, \(1\) unsigned, one-sided \(p=0.0352\) on the eight signed rows; the round entry's "six, all six optimistic" reads \(5\) of \(6\), \(p=0.1094\), not significant (READ V16_CALIBRATION.md:85-110; MISTAKES.md:2037-2100, D-7); the Wilson interval on the optimism fraction \([0.5291,0.9776]\) excludes \(0.5\) and fixes nothing else (READ docs/sources/design/design_falsify.md §0.2). Mechanism. D-7, L-SIGN, D-CALIB, M-2, L-G2, M-7. Kill — an audit of the appended column, not a refusal at the file, because a row refused at the file never enters the artefact the kill reads. A row in the column whose counter field is empty; a denominator chosen after the audit; a shrink factor fitted at fewer than eight rows (D-CALIB-3). The earlier wording — "a row filed without its counter, refused at the file, never discounted (D-CALIB-2)" — was satisfied by construction: the refusal it named removes the row before the column is written, so no row the kill could read ever carries an empty counter, and the gate fires on nothing (V-10, V-11). The refusal is retained as the upstream control and is now written into the instrument that performs it — 04.9's adjudicator specification gains "refuses any calibration row whose counter field is empty or absent", which it did not carry and which no other instrument of this book carried either (P-4) — while the kill is the downstream audit, observable on the artefact. Instrument: one read of the counter cell of every row of the appended column, V16_CALIBRATION.md in the working tree (RUN this session, ls V16_CALIBRATION.md succeeds; \(232\) lines, \(14\) lines matching counter case-insensitively), plus the adjudicator's refusal log for rows that never entered — the log being NOT MEASURED — needs the arena adjudicator and its frozen prediction file atresults/arena/PREDICTIONS.sha256` (RUNthis session,ls results/arenareadsNo such file or directory). **The audit is a read, not a test**, so 04.18's prose-coupling policy — which forbids a *test* from opening a.mdoutsideresults/— does not bind it and the two verses do not contradict each other. Price $0$ GPU-s. **Planted negative, two-way and on the artefact:** a row appended to the column with itscountercell empty, written directly and bypassing the adjudicator, must be reported by the audit — the known-bad case the kill's own condition instantiates and the case the upstream refusal by construction cannot produce; and a row carrying a counter of equal specificity must not be reported, which is the must-not-fire half. The upstream refusal keeps its own separate control: a bare prediction submitted to the file must be refused by the adjudicator (04.9), which is a statement about the file and not about the column. **If killed — link 1.** The offending row is VOID and the column's count excludes it; the sign test re-runs on the remainder. *Hypotheses:* rows are appended, never edited, so the VOID mark is a new row withsupersedes. *Evidence:* the R11 precedent — the round entry's six versus the table's nine, where the dropped rows changed $p$ from $0.1094$ to $0.0352$ (READV16_CALIBRATION.md:96-104`). Kill: fewer than eight scored rows remain — no rate is quoted, only the count; price \(0\) GPU-s. Terminal. "The column is a count with signs, never a rate, until eight scored rows exist, and its counter rule is audited on the appended column rather than asserted from a refusal no instrument of this book performed until 04.9's adjudicator specification was made to carry it."

docs.title: 04.18 — The test policy: tests assert code, journals and results/, never prose (B3)
docs.text: Statement. A test may assert a value computed by repository code, a record in a journal under results/, or a hash of a file the test itself produces; a test may not open a prose document, assert a line number of a document, or assert an anchor string inside a document. The line that decides: a test file is prose-coupled iff it names a path ending in .md outside results/ or asserts an integer as a line number of any file it does not generate. Prose-coupled tests are moved out of the collected tree, never edited into passing, and their count is printed beside the suite's. Hypotheses. The pattern file is a permanent object, not working-tree state. The deleted round documents are the rows marked D in git diff --name-status 99777ab c71527a restricted to root-level .md — \(244\) paths, fixed by two commit shas and reproducible from any checkout forever. The earlier definition ("the set marked D in git status --short") was struck because it is empty at c71527a: RUN this session, git status --short returns exactly \(2\) lines, M README.md and ?? docs/canon/, and \(0\) rows marked D, so the pattern file was empty and the Kill's grep read \(0\) unconditionally — a kill satisfied by construction (V-10, V-11) resting on uncommitted state that does not reproduce (P-2). The selector is the file's basename. Evidence. The whole census is re-run at a named commit and printed as RUN @ c71527a (git rev-parse HEAD reads c71527a64687043f2afa1667fe6485cc71022179). git diff --name-status 99777ab c71527a reads \(350\) rows marked D, of which \(244\) are root-level .md documents (the round reports) — the one number that survived from the earlier reading — and \(60\) match (^|/)test_[^/]*\.py$. The earlier claim "\(0\) test files are deleted" is false and is struck: sixty test files were removed between the pin and c71527a, and the surviving suite is smaller for it — tests/**/test_*.py reads \(291\) at 99777ab and \(239\) at c71527a (and \(239\) in the working tree), a net loss of \(52\) files (git ls-tree -r --name-only <sha> | grep -E '^tests/(.*/)?test_[^/]*\.py$' | wc -l). Against the \(244\)-path pattern file, grep -rlF -f deleted_docs.txt tests --include='*.py' reads \(120\) — not \(187\) — of which \(108\) are test_*.py; of those \(108\), \(43\) also read lines (splitlines|readlines|read_text|open(); \(32\) test_*.py carry a literal .md:NNN; \(71\) test_*.py read results/ or a .jsonl, and \(39\) of those name no deleted document. Root collection, quoted with its commit and its interpreter versions, because the count does not reproduce across sessions and the book must not carry it forward as a constant. RUN this session, python -m pytest --collect-only -q at HEAD c71527a (git rev-parse HEAD reads c71527a64687043f2afa1667fe6485cc71022179, working tree M README.md and ?? docs/canon/ only) on CPython 3.11.9, pytest 9.0.3, torch 2.14.0+cpu, numpy 2.4.6, reads 2626 tests collected, 17 errors, reproduced on three consecutive invocations (elapsed \(13.24\) s, \(24.19\) s, \(13.91\) s — the elapsed figure is not part of the reading and is not a number this book carries). The two earlier readings are printed beside it rather than replaced silently: 2971 tests collected, 26 errors (the verse as first written) and 2580 tests collected, 22 errors (the batch-3 repair, and the figure MARS re-read at 19.31s). Three different counts at one commit on one box is the number's own evidence class: the collection count is a function of the installed environment's import failures (B1: torchvision circular import, transformers.PreTrainedModel, ripser/persim against numpy 1) and not of the tree alone, so fewer errors collect more tests and the pair moves together — \(26\) errors at \(2971\), \(22\) at \(2580\), \(17\) at \(2626\). The count therefore moves and is never carried forward: every quotation of a collected count in this canon — including link 2's own suite count below — is re-read at assembly against the commit and the interpreter versions then in force, and a count quoted without both is struck (P-1, M-16). The counts that are pinned to commits and do reproduce — the \(350\) deletions, the \(244\) root .md, the \(60\) test_*.py, the \(291\to239\) survivors, the \(120/108/43/32/71/39\) census — are the ones this book carries, because git diff and git ls-tree at two shas are the same in every checkout and pytest --collect-only is not. tests/gate0/ holds \(15\) test_*.py files, of which test_g05_data.py is 31 passed in 0.73s (RUN, 04.7). The CHARTER's own count reads \(56\) (READ docs/canon/CHARTER.md §5 B3) under an unstated selector; the selector above is the one this verse freezes, and every count in this paragraph is pinned to 99777ab → c71527a rather than to a working tree. The pattern the policy replaces: the wing manifest's anchor check test_every_frozen_citation_resolves_at_head, \(20\) passed, \(1\) failed at 207e7b9 (READ V20_R15_WING_MANIFEST.md:148-160 @ 99777ab); line-reference drift READ MISTAKES.md:364-374 (P-6: cite the symbol, not the line). Mechanism. P-6, P-5, P-3, V-26 (a marginal count of green nodes is not coverage), V-6, V-10 and V-11 (a kill whose pattern file is empty reads \(0\) by construction), P-1, P-2 (a census of uncommitted working-tree state does not reproduce). Kill. After the move, grep -rlF -f deleted_docs.txt tests --include='*.py' reads above \(0\) against the \(244\)-path pattern file built from git diff --name-status 99777ab c71527a, or any collected test opens a .md outside results/; or a moved test is edited to pass against a stub document. The pattern file is named by two shas, so the kill is decidable in any checkout at any date and cannot be emptied by a clean working tree. Instrument: the two greps above and pytest --collect-only, price \(0\) GPU-s. Planted negative, in both directions, and with no line number in it. One test that opens docs/canon/CHARTER.md — a path ending in .md outside results/ — is written into the collected tree and must be caught by the second grep; the selector fires on a known-coupled test. The plant carries no assertion about that file's length, and the earlier form of it, "one test that asserts docs/canon/CHARTER.md has \(317\) lines", is struck twice over: the figure was wrong (RUN this session, wc -l docs/canon/CHARTER.md reads \(316\), the file ending without a trailing newline so a line-counting read returns \(317\) and wc -l returns \(316\) — the ambiguity is itself the P-6 mechanism this policy exists against), it carried no evidence class, and the plant's job is to name a .md outside results/, which the selector's first half decides, not to assert a true number. And the \(244\)-path pattern file must read \(120\) today (RUN @ c71527a), a non-zero count, which is the must-fire calibration the empty git status file could never give. The plant is NOT MEASURED — needs the test-policy migration of 05 REPAIRS, and this book writes no test: 04.13's own Kill strikes "any plant that exists only in a script's print (NAMED)", and a plant this book describes and never writes is NAMED by that rule, so it is marked and priced there rather than claimed here. Its verification, when 05 REPAIRS writes it, is one RUN of the second grep against the planted file returning that file's path. If killed — link 1. The collected tree is restricted by an explicit list (testpaths naming only directories whose files pass the selector); everything else is tests/attic/ and uncollected. Hypotheses: the selector is run on every file before it is listed; the pattern file is the \(244\)-path commit-pinned one. Evidence: the \(120/239\) census above ($108$ of themtest_.py) is the file list the move starts from,RUN @ c71527a. *Kill:* atests/attic/file collected — the configuration is wrong and the suite's count is not a count; decided bypytest --collect-onlyat $0$ GPU-s, cheaper than the grep pair because it is one command. **If killed — link 2.** The suite that ships is the **$39$-file** subset oftest_.pyreadingresults/or a.jsonland naming no deleted document, plus every test undertests/gate0/($15$ files;test_g05_data.pyis $31$ passed); the number of collected tests is printed in the book that cites the suite, **re-read at assembly against the commit and the interpreter versions then in force and never carried forward from this page** — the root collection read $2626$ with $17$ errors this session atc71527aonCPython 3.11.9/pytest 9.0.3/torch 2.14.0+cpu/numpy 2.4.6, and read $2580/22$ and $2971/26$ in two earlier sessions at the same tree. *Kill:* a quoted test count exceeding the collected count **at the commit and interpreter the quotation names**, or a quoted count naming neither — struck as P-1. **Terminal.** "The test count quoted anywhere in the canon is the count of tests that assert code and journals; no test asserts a sentence. The census is pinned to99777ab → c71527aand reads $350$ deletions, $244$ of them root.mdand **$60$ of themtest_.py**; the suite fell from $291$ to $239$test_.py` across those two commits, and that loss is printed rather than described as \(0\)."

docs.title: 04.19 — The magnitude interval and the two registrations (B23)
docs.text: Statement. The magnitude support is registered per base, not once. On the path-product base \(W_{ij}=\prod_{k=j+1}^{i}m_ke^{i\theta_k}\) the interval is closed, \(m_k\in[0,1]\), because pathProd_eq_zero_iff carries no hypothesis and \(m_c=0\) is the F0 cut; on the exponential prefix-scan base \(W=\exp(\mathrm{scan}\,g)\), \(g=\log m\), the interval is half-open, \(m_k\in(0,1]\), because no prefix scan represents a zero gate and \(\log0\) is junk in the scan. BED-M's Rademacher draw \(a\in\{-1,0,+1\}\) has magnitude support \(\{0,1\}\); on the closed base \(100\) per cent of its entries are admitted; on the half-open base \(0\) of \(2{,}048\) sequences satisfy \(\forall k,\ 0<m_k\), so every theorem stated on that base is decoration on BED-M and the census says so. The two registrations are inverse only when written for one base; written per base they do not meet. On BED-S at the softmax corner \(m\equiv1\) and the question does not arise. Hypotheses. The base is declared in the manifest (g parametrisation id, 04.15); the census prints the fraction of draws admitted at the quantifier level the theorem uses (per sequence for a \(\forall k\) hypothesis). Evidence. V-25's census on BED-M e3_t2: support \(\{-1.0,0.0,+1.0\}\); entries with \(a>0\) \(2{,}077/131{,}072=1.5846\) per cent; \(a=0\) \(96.875\) per cent; sequences satisfying \(\forall k,\ 0<a_k\): \(0\) of \(2{,}048\), structural because a[:, :head + 1] = 0.0 (READ MISTAKES.md:1954-2036); the \(\varepsilon\)-sweep \(\varepsilon=0\to\) nan against \(2.44\times10^{-15}\) at \(\varepsilon=10^{-9}\) (READ V15_ARM_PHASE.md:303-308 @ 99777ab); pathProd_eq_zero_iff at lean/CEQ/V16Domain.lean:129 and no_prefix_scan_represents_a_zero_gate at :165 (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §2.1 Definition 1); the closed-versus-half-open filing and D-R3 READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §4.4. Mechanism. V-25, D-R3, V-22, M-20 (two registrations that never met), P-11. Kill. A theorem cited as a train gate on a base whose census admits \(0\) per cent of draws at its quantifier level — the gate is blocked and the theorem is inadmissible until restated on the support that exists. Instrument: clause 10 of 04.2's numbered admission block — "the per-base admitted fraction at the quantifier level each magnitude theorem uses (04.19), printed per base" — which is this verse's own line and needs no extension. The earlier pointer, "the census line 15 of 04.2", named a line that does not exist: 04.2's block has eleven numbered clauses and no fifteenth, so the instrument this Kill named was unreachable as written (P-4, P-6). Price \(0\). Planted negative: the BED-M e3_t2 census on the half-open base must print \(0\) of \(2{,}048\) — the known-empty domain fires the block. If killed — link 1. The theorem is restated on the closed base with magnitudes and circle phases (the v16 restatement), and the census re-run. Hypotheses: the restated theorem's hypothesis is a predicate on \(m\in[0,1]\) with no positivity clause. Evidence: v16's #2 was re-stated on \([0,1]\) magnitudes and circle phases for exactly this reason, and the pathProd_* clauses admit 3 of 3 BED-M values (READ MISTAKES.md:2020-2036; docs/sources/design/design_instrument.md row K). Kill: the restated theorem's hypothesis still admits \(0\) per cent — the base, not the interval, is wrong for the bed; price \(0\) GPU-s, the same census. Terminal. "Every magnitude theorem is stated with its base and its admitted fraction; no gate rests on an interval its corpus never enters."

docs.title: 04.20 — The skyline cells: one FOUND, two with settings and no cell (B11)
docs.text: Statement. Four skylines are read beside every bed with their settings frozen before the arena. The first two are the same depth at two parameter counts, and only the second can carry an A2 sentence (04.9 clause 3): the depth-\(\lfloor\log_2t^\star\rfloor+2\) softmax stack (\(5\) at \(t^\star=8\)) at full width and unmatched parameters, which must be FOUND at the design point and whose number is printed as \(\Delta_{\rm sky}\), a control satisfying R-SKY and licensing no A2 sentence; and the matched-parameter skyline of 04.9 clause 3b — the same depth \(5\) at reduced width, the width fixed before any draw as the largest per-layer width whose total count lands within \(0.0960\) per cent of the shape's, with sky_width and the exact params_per_arm printed — which is the only arm A2 is read against, and whose width is NOT MEASURED — needs the reduced-width parameter count once the $[m,K+2]$ head's count is fixed, $0$ GPU-s. Then two skylines with no cell, and — until this repair — no instrument and no price either, which is why B11's skyline-cells row is closed for one of three and the census table now says so. Each is named with the instrument it needs and with what its price is and is not: | skyline | setting frozen here | instrument it needs | price | |---|---|---|---| | depth-\(5\) full width | depth \(\lfloor\log_2t^\star\rfloor+2=5\) at \(d_{\rm model}=16\), unmatched parameters | FOUND at the design point; the depth-\(5\) cell of docs/PLAN.md S-35 | \(\approx7.6\) s per cell [ASSUMED linear in depth], \(\approx64.8\) s at eight seeds | | depth-\(5\) matched width | depth \(5\) at the reduced width of 04.9 clause 3b | one parameter-count arithmetic pass, then the same S-35 cell at that width | width NOT MEASURED — needs the reduced-width parameter count; the pass is \(0\) GPU-s; the cell is \(\approx64.8\) s at eight seeds on the same basis | | wide constant depth | depth \(1\) at width \(=n_{\rm nodes}=64\) | NOT MEASURED — needs a width-$64$ constant-depth arm at matched parameters (one make_arm branch at a second width, one optimizer path, one field emit, on 04.14's arm_pl basis of \(41\)–\(130\) GPU-s per branch) | build \(41\)–\(130\) GPU-s, \(1\) evening, DERIVED from 04.14's per-branch route; the per-cell run time is NOT MEASURED — needs one timed cell of the width-$64$ arm, and the reason is printed: both cell bases this book carries (\(1.680\) s shape, \(1.524\) s softmax) are at \(d_{\rm model}=16\) and the only scaling law it registers is [ASSUMED linear in depth], which prices a depth change and prices no width change at all | | CoT decoder | \(t^\star=8\) decode steps at the registered geometry | NOT MEASURED — needs a CoT decode harness at $t^\star$ decode steps (a sequential-decode loop, a per-step journal emit and a stop rule, none of which exists in the tree) | build \(41\)–\(130\) GPU-s, \(1\) evening, on the same per-branch basis; the per-cell run time is NOT MEASURED — needs one timed decode cell, since a decode cell is \(8\) sequential forward passes per query and no forward-pass-per-decode-step figure is registered anywhere in this book | At \(d_{\rm model}=16<s=64\) the wide stack has no matched-parameter instance at the registered geometry, so even once built it is a control at unmatched parameters and licenses no A2 sentence, exactly as the full-width depth-\(5\) arm does. A price with no basis is not a price, so the two run-time cells are marked NOT MEASURED rather than extrapolated from a depth law that does not cover a width change or a decode loop — the P-1 defect this book struck three times over in 04.11. The depth is a choice by analogy with Thm 4.2 of sanford-2024-logdepth, whose task is \(\mathrm{hop}_k\) and not the committor; the reduction is book 01's and until it is written the depth row is a control, not a theorem. Hypotheses. Both depth-5 arms run on the same byte-identical draws and journal as the matched arms; the full-width one's parameter count is printed as unmatched, which is exactly why it is \(\Delta_{\rm sky}\) and not an A2 arm; the reduced-width one's count is printed and must land within \(0.0960\) per cent of the shape's or it is unmatched too and no A2 number exists on the bed. Evidence. Thm 4.2 CITED [V] sanford-2024-logdepth; the width skyline CITED [V] yehudai-2025-depthwidth; CoT CITED [V] merrill-2024-cot; the iteration argument CITED [V] wang-2024-incontext-td, xie-2026-softmax-rl (abstracts); the reduction NOT FOUND (READ docs/sources/sweep/sweep_expressivity.md §3.5); price \(\approx7.6\) s per depth-5 cell [ASSUMED linear in depth], \(\approx64.8\) s at eight seeds (READ docs/PLAN.md §5.7). Mechanism. R-SKY, D-1, P-10, V-25, D-7, P-4, Ruling 3 (A2 is at matched parameters or it is not A2), V-17. Kill (Bet D) — one-sided, with its subject named, because the two-sided form fired on the A2 result this canon exists to obtain. The comparison is \(\mathrm{acc}_{\rm sky}-\mathrm{acc}_{\rm shape}\), read against the matched-parameter skyline of clause 3b and against no other arm, at \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at the realised \(\sigma_d\) (04.9 clause 7; NOT MEASURED — needs $\sigma_d$ from 04.21 step (5)), and the two signs are named rather than left to a reader: - the skyline short of the shape by more than \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) is the A2 reading and is not a kill — the skyline's learned hops fall short of the exact solve by more than \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\), which is CHARTER §1's definition of A2 word for word; it is logged with its sign and it fires nothing; - the skyline ahead of the shape by more than \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) kills Bet D and withdraws A2 on the bed — "one operator" carries no accuracy sentence at all against a depth stack at matched parameters, and the bed needs something the one-solve construction does not supply. The earlier wording named neither subject ("short says the bed needs something the hop construction does not supply; ahead says 'one operator' carries no accuracy sentence") and stood at \(|\cdot|>\mathrm{MDE}_N\) in either direction; under the shape-as-subject reading its "short" clause is the A2 result, so the kill fired on the very number the canon is built to produce (V-10). 04.6 link 1 uses the same two words with the skyline as subject — "the matched-parameter skyline ahead by more than \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) … 'one operator' carries no accuracy sentence at all" — and that is the reading this verse now carries, so the two verses read one way. Also: a depth chosen after the arena, or a width chosen after the arena, strikes the row (M-2). Instrument: the depth-5 cell of docs/PLAN.md S-35 at both widths. Planted negative: a depth-1 stack labelled as the skyline must fall short by more than \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) on a bed with \(t^\star=8\) — if it does not, the bed is static (04.5). If killed — link 1. The depth ladder \(\{3,5,7\}\) is run at \(t^\star=8\), each depth at its own matched width, and the smallest depth inside \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at the realised \(\sigma_d\) is reported as the skyline; price \(3\times64.8\) s [ASSUMED], 1 evening. Hypotheses: the ladder and the three widths are registered before the run (M-2), never chosen after. Evidence: the same three depths are the registered skylines at \(t^\star=2/8/32\) (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §6 A.4); the three matched widths NOT MEASURED — needs the parameter-count pass of 04.9 clause 3b. Kill: no depth inside \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at the realised \(\sigma_d\) — the hop construction does not cover the bed, and A2 is undefined on it; more decisive than the single cell because it rules out every registered depth at once. Terminal. "The full-width depth-5 row is a measured control at unmatched depth and unmatched parameters, printed as \(\Delta_{\rm sky}\) and licensing no A2 sentence; the matched-width row A2 requires has no width, no count and no cell, so no A2 number exists anywhere in this book; the wide constant-depth arm and the CoT decoder have a named instrument each and a build price each (\(41\)–\(130\) GPU-s, \(1\) evening, per branch) and no run-time price at all, because this book registers no width law and no decode law to price them with; so B11's skyline-cells row is closed for the depth skyline only — one of the four registered skylines carries a cell, one carries an arithmetic pass, and two carry a build price with an unmeasured run time; and the sentence 'depth \(\lfloor\log_2t^\star\rfloor+2\) suffices' is not asserted for the committor."

docs.title: 04.21 — The first BED-S cell: what eight seeds produce, in what order (B5)
docs.text: Statement. No CEQ arm has been trained — and the sentence is stated on a discriminator, never on the phrase, because the record count for the file the repository itself calls a CEQ arm contradicts the phrase. A CEQ-arm cell is one whose kind is arm_ceq and which carries boundary_sets, goal_set and sink_set with their sha256s (04.15's field list); RUN this session, both counts read \(0\) across all of results/ — grep -rn 'arm_ceq' --include='*.py' . returns \(0\) source lines and grep -rl 'boundary_sets' results --include='*.jsonl' returns \(0\) files. The \(425\) records the kind census reads under arm_smprime are not counter-evidence and are not CEQ-arm cells: arm_smprime is the record's complex-chain lane — NAME = "arm_smprime" at READ ceq/arm_smprime.py:77, emitting "kind": NAME at :346, its records carrying "task": "chain_label_complex" / e3_t2 — and not one of the \(425\) declares a boundary set, which is the discriminator and the whole of it. Without that discriminator printed, neither this Statement nor 04.15's "zero shape-lane cells" is falsifiable, and a reader holding the \(425\)-record count against the phrase would be right (FOUND-not-NAMED, V-7, P-1). BED-S has no cell, no realised sd, no measured \(t^\star\), no \(I(X_{\le k};a^\star)\). The first eight seeds are run in this order and produce these objects before any bet is scored: (1) the census of 04.2 admits; (2) the binds of 04.13 pass through the front door — every plant of 04.13's table, whose numbers are float instances on random logits and are marked NOT MEASURED at the front door until this step, is reproduced as bed.build → arm.forward → journal row → verdict() on one admitted draw each, nine bind rows, priced \(\approx9\times1.680\approx15.1\) s [ASSUMED] on the arm_smprime cell basis, \(0.5\) evening; no bind is admissible and no verse may cite a bind number until this step's journal exists; (3) the \(\hat\gamma\)-free controls of 04.11 run before the shape — the 0-hop MLP, the 1-hop softmax, majority, random, predict-the-mean, the depth-\(\lfloor\log_2t^\star\rfloor+2\) skyline of 04.20 and InfSA-Neumann-\(16\) — every one of which is defined without reference to any trained quantity, in the randomised interleaved order of 04.10 recorded per cell; (4) the shape runs, producing \(\hat\gamma\) per seed; (4a) the \(\hat\gamma\)-dependent controls run after the shape, because 04.11's own Hypotheses define them only once \(\hat\gamma\) exists — ChaCAL-diag and ChaCAL-with-sink are read at the shape's trained \(\hat\gamma\), so scheduling them at step (3) would schedule a contract behind an unreached round (D-4) and would freeze a dial after the data (M-2). Their order and the inherited \(\hat\gamma\) they were run at are printed in the manifest (04.15's gamma block: init, final \(\hat\gamma\), \(\Lambda\), verdict, plus the seed whose \(\hat\gamma\) was inherited), so the sequential dependency is auditable and no reader mistakes a post-shape control for a pre-registered one; (5) the adjudicator of 04.9 fills, from the journal alone, \(\sigma_d\) per scored statistic, \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at that realised \(\sigma_d\) with \(N\) chosen by 04.9 clause 7's rule — never a placeholder \(\mathrm{MDE}_8\) — \(t^\star\) read off the hop ladder, \(\hat\gamma\) and \(\Lambda\) per seed, \(\|\hat P-P_{\rm env}\|_\infty\) per seed, and only then scores Bets A–H against their counters. Hypotheses. L-LEAN: the [M] targets of Proposition 1 and Proposition 5 build before step (4); the device is the certified one, with the four determinism quantities filled (solve_triangular forward and backward bitwise over \(8\) repeats under strict mode, RUN[NEPTUNE], no documented guarantee). Evidence. "There is no result": READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §8; every BED-S number in the record is a floor formula or a design constant (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md §6 A.13); the \(\gamma\)-pinning null on the boundary, \(\tfrac12\chi^2_0+\tfrac12\chi^2_1\) at \(95\) per cent \(=2.7055\), MOVED at \(\Lambda>\ln4096=8.318\) (RUN[J]; citation owed); the arena price \(\approx3.3\) GPU-min DERIVED; the \(14\)-evening critical path (READ docs/PLAN.md §5.4). Mechanism. M-3, M-2 (a threshold frozen as a rule, and a dial never frozen after the data), L-LEAN, D-4 (a \(\hat\gamma\)-dependent control is staged behind the shape, never started before it), P-1, V-11. Kill. Any number quoted for BED-S before step (5) writes \(\sigma_d\) into the journal; or a bet scored against any placeholder \(\mathrm{MDE}_8\) — \(0.011677\), \(0.039827\), \(0.057971\), \(0.126238\) or any other row of 04.9's table — instead of \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at the realised cell; or a \(\hat\gamma\)-dependent control journalled at step (3) rather than step (4a), which would record a dial chosen after the data. The forbidden thresholds and the six kills that used to carry them are named, so the prohibition is not a rule with no referent: the placeholder number is struck from 04.3's floor comparison, 04.4 link 1's R0 clause, 04.5's half-width clause, 04.6's Bet E and link 1, 04.7's majority-sign clause, 04.11's K-E1 and 04.20's Bet D, each of which now reads \(\mathrm{MDE}_N\) at the realised \(\sigma_d\) under 04.9 clause 7 and carries NOT MEASURED — needs $\sigma_d$ from 04.21 step (5) beside it. Instrument: the adjudicator's predictions_hash check and its refusal below \(8\) seeds — both NOT MEASURED — needs the arena adjudicator and its frozen prediction file atresults/arena/PREDICTIONS.sha256` (RUNthis session,ls results/arenareadsNo such file or directory; the construction is priced in 05 REPAIRS) — and a grep of the scored journal for a literal $\mathrm{MDE}_8$ constant, which is the one half of the instrument that runs today. Price $0$. Planted negative: a journal with $7$ seeds must return INSUFFICIENT; a duplicated seed must count once; a bet row written with the literal threshold $0.039827$ must be refused by the grep, and the same row written as "$\mathrm{MDE}_N$ at $\sigma_d$ from this journal" must pass — the two-way calibration the prohibition needs. **If killed — link 1.** The offending number is struck with asupersedesrow; the cell is not re-run, the journal is re-read. *Hypotheses:* the journal carries per-seed statistics (04.15'seval_traceand the scored columns). *Evidence:* the adjudicator computes $\sigma_d$ from journals only and never from a table (READdocs/PLAN.md` S-61). Kill: the re-read still lacks \(\sigma_d\) — the cell did not journal its per-seed statistics and is NAMED (04.14); price \(0\) GPU-s. Terminal. "BED-S has no cell; every number about it is a specification."

What book 04 closes of B27, and what it does not. CHARTER §5 assigns B27 to two books, and this book closes exactly one half of it: the instrument half of the chess use, in 04.7 — the five hygiene guards with their planted violations (RUN this session, 31 passed in 0.73s), the by-game split and FEN dedupe, the rollout label at the frozen \(h=8\), its per-constraint base-rate floor and the join-hit census with its discard rule. The market half — the state as order book and price path, contracts as absorbing sets, the market-implied baseline as the floor, the look-ahead guard and the by-event split with its planted violation — appears in no verse of this book, registers no instrument here, and is closed in 09 alone: 09.21 (the state), 09.22 (contracts as absorbing sets), 09.23a–09.23b (the market-implied probability as the registered floor), 09.24 (Brier and log score against it, with the near-efficiency counter under D-CALIB), 09.25 and 09.29b (BED-P-L and BED-P-N), 09.28 (leakage, look-ahead and by-event guards) and 09.32 (the market domain census). This book registers no market bed because CHARTER §6 gives book 04 three beds — BED-S, BED-J and the chess witness — and none of them is a market; duplicating 09's market instruments here would put one object under two owners, which is the M-20 mechanism (two registrations that never met) this book files B23 against. The loss is stated rather than covered: if 09's market verses are struck, B27's market half is closed by nothing in this canon, and no verse of book 04 can carry it — the row above is then open on its market half and the sentence in force is 04.7's Terminal for chess and silence for markets.

docs.title: Limits (collected once)
docs.text: No GPU exists in this session (torch 2.14.0+cpu); every GPU-second above is READ from the certified record at the pin and none was re-measured. Every RUN here is a grep, a git status, a pytest invocation or a one-line Python read of an existing module; none computes a statistic. The prose-coupling census depends on its selector (basename of a deleted root document), which differs from the CHARTER's unstated selector that read \(56\); both counts are printed, and the whole census is now pinned to 99777ab → c71527a rather than to a working tree — \(350\) deletions, \(244\) root .md, \(60\) test_*.py, \(291\to239\) surviving test_*.py, \(120\) files under tests/ naming a deleted document (\(108\) of them test_*.py), \(43\) of those reading lines, \(32\) carrying .md:NNN, \(71\) reading results/ or .jsonl of which \(39\) name no deleted document. The root collection count is the one number in this census that does not reproduce and is therefore never carried forward: it reads \(2626\) with \(17\) errors this session at c71527a on CPython 3.11.9 / pytest 9.0.3 / torch 2.14.0+cpu / numpy 2.4.6, reproduced on three consecutive invocations, against \(2580/22\) and \(2971/26\) in two earlier sessions at the same tree; the count is a function of the environment's import failures (B1) and not of the tree, fewer errors collecting more tests, so every quotation of it in this canon is re-read at assembly with its commit and its interpreter versions and a quotation carrying neither is struck. docs.text:

Flaw (verbatim). B27 is assigned to book 04 by the CHARTER and is not closed; the market half of the author's two uses appears nowhere in the book. Mechanism (verbatim). L-DOM, B27 Number (verbatim). CHARTER §5 B27 owning book: "09 CHESS_AND_MARKETS, 04". The census table lists ten rows and does not name B27. RUN this session: grep -ci market 04_BEDS_AND_INSTRUMENTS.md reads 0. replacement_survives (verbatim). false Required repair (verbatim). Add a verse registering the prediction-market bed as an instrument (state as order book and price path, contracts as absorbing sets, the market-implied baseline as the floor, the look-ahead guard and the by-event split with its planted violation), or add a B27 row to the census table naming 09 as the owner and stating exactly which half of B27 book 04 closes (the chess witness's hygiene guards, 04.7). Severity (verbatim). strike

Repair applied — Census rows closed, Preface. The second of the two routes the required repair licenses is taken, and the reason is stated rather than assumed: CHARTER §6 gives book 04 three beds — BED-S, BED-J and the chess witness — and none of them is a market, while CHARTER §6 gives book 09 the market use in full; registering a market bed here would put one object under two owners, which is the M-20 mechanism (two registrations that never met) this book files B23 against, and would risk two books contradicting each other on one bed's floor. A B27 row is added to the census table reading "the two uses — chess half only", closed by 04.7 and naming the owner as "09 CHESS_AND_MARKETS, 04" per CHARTER §5. A paragraph beneath the table states exactly what this book closes (04.7's five hygiene guards with their planted violations, RUN 31 passed in 0.73s; the by-game split and FEN dedupe; the \(h=8\) rollout label; its per-constraint base-rate floor; the join-hit census with its discard rule) and exactly what it does not: the market half — the state as order book and price path, contracts as absorbing sets, the market-implied baseline as the floor, the look-ahead guard and the by-event split with its planted violation — appears in no verse of this book, and is closed in 09 alone, at 09.21, 09.22, 09.23a, 09.23b, 09.24, 09.25, 09.28, 09.29b and 09.32, each named. The Preface's "Ten census rows are closed here" is corrected to ten in full plus B27 on its chess half. Because replacement_survives reads false and a census table is not a verse and carries no If-killed chain, the loss is carried by the row itself: the paragraph states that if 09's market verses are struck, B27's market half is closed by nothing in this canon and no verse of book 04 can carry it, the row is then open on that half, and the sentence in force is 04.7's Terminal for chess and silence for markets.

Repair applied — 04.11, 04.6, 04.5, Kills table. The first route is taken: no overhead term exists that carries \(52\) or \(34\), so both are struck and the arithmetic is printed at every site. 04.11's Evidence now reads \(3\times8\times1.680+4.0=44.32\) s for three arms at eight seeds, with the \(4.0\) s named as the arena's fixed set-up overhead carried at the same [ASSUMED] class as 04.9's \(7\times8\times1.680+4.0\approx98\) s, and states that no overhead term carries the missing \(7.7\) s. The pair price is printed as \(2\times8\times1.680+4.0=30.88\approx30.9\) s and replaces \(\approx34\) s in 04.6's Bet E instrument, in 04.5's link 2 and in the "Kills, cheapest first" row for 04.6. 04.11's K-E1 clause, which cited the three-arm \(\approx52\) s for a two-arm pair, is repriced to \(\approx30.9\) s with the arithmetic beside it, and its closing sentence ("the price of reaching it is link 2's, not …") carries the corrected figure. 04.6's Bet E instrument is additionally reclassed from [FITTED + RUN] to [ASSUMED], on A-2's ground: neither arm of that pair is FOUND on BED-J. docs.title: A-36 · verse 04.11 · severity repair
docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). A DERIVED price is printed with no steps and is wrong by 12.6x under the only derivation the verse states. Mechanism (verbatim). P-1 (CHARTER §2: DERIVED (steps)) Number (verbatim). "InfSA-16 \(\approx5.12\) s per cell DERIVED from the \(25.409\) ms hop": \(16\times25.409\,\mathrm{ms}=0.407\) s, a factor \(12.6\) below \(5.12\). Book 06 supplies the missing factor ("InfSA-16's step is \(0.034133\) s", 06_PREDICTIONS.md:349): \(150\times0.034133=5.12\) s. 04.9's \(\approx3.3\) GPU-min arena price rests on the 5.12 figure. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Print the derivation in this verse: 150 steps per cell x 0.034133 s/step = 5.12 s, and give the 150-step budget its own evidence class. Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.11. The derivation is printed and the class is corrected. The verse now states that \(16\times25.409\,\mathrm{ms}=0.407\) s, a factor \(12.6\) below \(5.12\) s, so the source's own words "DERIVED from the \(25.409\) ms hop microbenchmark" (READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md:1926 @ 99777ab) do not reproduce and a DERIVED class with no steps is a P-1 defect. The one multiplication that does reproduce is printed: \(150\) steps per cell \(\times\ 0.034133\) s/step \(=5.11995\approx5.12\) s (DERIVED, one multiplication). The \(150\)-step budget carries its own evidence class, READ scale/e_ladder.py:140 (steps=150), the record's registered cell length; the \(0.034133\) s/step is \(5.12/150\) read back out of the source figure and is named as such, so the pair is not passed off as an independent measurement. The \(\approx5.12\) s therefore enters this book as READ docs/CEQ_SHAPE.md:1926 @ 99777ab, unreproduced, on top of the [ASSUMED] cell basis of A-2, which is how book 06 reads it at 06.28 — the two books now agree on the class as well as the number. 04.9's \(\approx3.3\) GPU-min is shown to rest on it, with its arithmetic printed (\(98+8\times7.6+8\times5.12=199.8\) s), and inherits the tag. Limits records the reclassification once.

Hypotheses fix \(s=64\), so \(|T|\le63\). Evidence: "\(|T|^3/3=5.76\times10^{8}\) MACs at \(|T|=1200\)". At \(|T|=63\), \(|T|^3/3=8.33\times10^{4}\) MACs — \(6.9\times10^{3}\) times smaller. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Repair applied — 04.2 (already in force from an earlier batch; verified against this finding). 04.2's Evidence reads, verbatim in the book: "The oracle price at the registered geometry: \(s=64\) fixes \(|T|\le63\), so \(m\) factorisations of \(|T|^3/3=8.33\times10^{4}\) MACs each with \(m(K+2)=32\) right-hand sides, milliseconds per draw in float64 (DERIVED). The figure \(|T|^3/3=5.76\times10^{8}\) MACs holds at \(|T|=1200\) and is carried here only as a headroom note at that named geometry, \(6.9\times10^{3}\) times the registered one (DERIVED); no admission number rests on it." Both halves of the required repair are met — \(8.33\times10^4\) MACs and \(m(K+2)=32\) right-hand sides at the registered geometry, and \(|T|=1200\) retained only as a headroom note with its geometry named — and the arithmetic checks: \(63^3/3=83{,}349=8.33\times10^4\), \(8\times4=32\), \((5.76\times10^{8})/(8.33\times10^{4})=6.9\times10^{3}\). No further edit was owed and none was made; the finding is answered by the text quoted, not by an assertion that it was answered.

docs.text:

V-10, D-1 Number (verbatim). "or McNemar \(p>0.05\) against a 1-hop softmax on identical draws (K-H2)" — no subject. Under (shape, 1-hop softmax) the bed is declared static whenever the shape fails to separate from a 1-hop stack; under (0-hop MLP, 1-hop softmax) the clause says nothing about the shape. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Repair applied — 04.5 (already in force from an earlier batch; verified against this finding). 04.5's Statement reads, verbatim in the book: "or if McNemar between the 0-hop MLP and the 1-hop softmax reads \(p>0.05\) on identical draws (K-H2). The second clause names its pair because an unnamed pair is not decidable: under (0-hop MLP, 1-hop softmax) a null result says one hop buys nothing over none, which is the static-bed reading and the only reading this kill carries. docs.title: A-43 · verse 04.6 · severity repair
docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). The residual's printed conditioning factor is a 2-norm quantity attached to an infinity-norm score. Mechanism (verbatim). V-17, V-26 Number (verbatim). \(r(\hat q)=\|(I-Q_{\rm env})\hat q-R_{\rm env}\mathbb 1\|_\infty/\|R_{\rm env}\mathbb 1\|_\infty\) is an \(\infty\)-norm ratio; the DERIVED bound \(\sigma_{\min}\|e\|\le\|(I-\gamma P)e\|\le(1+\gamma)\|e\|\) and the "lower factor near \(0.06\)" are 2-norm. On \(|T|=9\) the conversion costs up to \(\sqrt9=3\) in each direction. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Print \(\|(I-Q_{\rm env})^{-1}\|_\infty\) beside \(r\) instead of \(\sigma_{\min}\), or restate \(r\) in the 2-norm so the printed factors bind it. Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.6 (already in force from an earlier batch; verified against this finding). The first route is taken. 04.6's Statement reads, verbatim in the book: "with \(\|(I-Q_{\rm env})^{-1}\|_\infty\) and \(\|I-Q_{\rm env}\|_\infty\) printed beside \(r\) — both in the \(\infty\)-norm \(r\) is written in. The 2-norm pair \(\sigma_{\min}\|e\|_2\le\|(I-\gamma P)e\|_2\le(1+\gamma)\|e\|_2\) and its 'lower factor near \(0.06\)' do not bind an \(\infty\)-norm ratio: on \(|T|=9\) the conversion costs up to \(\sqrt9=3\) in each direction, so a factor quoted at \(0.06\) in the 2-norm bounds an \(\infty\)-norm error only to within \(9\times\) (DERIVED from \(\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|_2\le\sqrt{|T|}\,\|x\|_\infty\)). The 2-norm factors are retained as a separate, labelled 2-norm remark and license no reading of \(r\)." The Evidence marks \(\|(I-Q_{\rm env})^{-1}\|_\infty\) as "NOT MEASURED — needs one read of the built chain, $0$ GPU-s on the bed's own generator", so the substitute factor carries a class rather than a value it does not have. No further edit was owed and none was made.

docs.title: A-44 · verse 04.7 · severity repair
docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). The capability channel's labels exist only for post-move FENs present in the evaluation shard, an availability-biased subset with no registered guard. Mechanism (verbatim). M-21, V-24 Number (verbatim). Hypotheses: "the evaluation shard streamed and pinned on one shard; the join by FEN". For an arbitrary candidate move \(a\) the post-move FEN need not appear in lichess/chess-evaluations (34.4 GB, UNPINNED_AWAITING_KAGGLE, results/k_data_manifest.json), so \(\operatorname{sign}\Delta\mathrm{eval}(\text{FEN},a)\) is missing for an unmeasured fraction of candidates and the argmin over \(m\) is not formable. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Add a census line printing the join-hit rate per candidate move and a rule that a query with any missing candidate is discarded, with the discard rate printed beside the cell. Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.7 (already in force from an earlier batch; verified against this finding). 04.7's Hypotheses read, verbatim in the book: "The join is availability-biased and is censused, not assumed: for an arbitrary candidate move \(a\) the post-move FEN need not appear in lichess/chess-evaluations at all, so \(\operatorname{sign}\Delta\mathrm{eval}(\text{FEN},a)\) is missing for an unmeasured fraction of candidates and the argmin over \(m\) is not formable on a query with a hole. A census line prints the join-hit rate per candidate move on every cell, and the rule is: a query with any missing candidate is discarded, with the discard rate printed beside the cell and beside every number the cell carries. The join-hit rate is NOT MEASURED — needs the pinned eval shard, so no argmin number on the capability channel exists before it is printed." The Kill carries the same clause ("any capability number quoted before the join-hit rate and its discard rate are printed … struck as P-1") and the planted negative is the holed query ("a query built with one candidate's post-move FEN deliberately absent from the joined shard must be discarded by the join census"). All three halves of the required repair — the census line, the discard rule, the printed rate — are in force; no further edit was owed and none was made.

docs.title: A-46 · verse 04.8 · severity repair
docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). The consequence head both refuses the no-change predictor and prints its error as a floor. Mechanism (verbatim). V-10, L-FLOOR Number (verbatim). Statement: "An arm emitting \(\Delta\hat z\equiv0\) makes the cosine \(0/0\) and is refused, not scored." The same row's floor column: "exact oracle \(0.0\); the no-change predictor's error printed". The no-change predictor is \(\Delta\hat z\equiv0\). replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Score the no-change predictor on the position-matched NRMSE vector alone (where it is well defined) and refuse it only on the cosine column, printing which columns the refusal covers. Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.8, 04.15. The refusal is made per column and its scope is printed. 04.8's Statement now reads: the refusal is per column "because a head that refuses an arm outright and prints that same arm's error as its floor refuses and scores one object at once (V-10, L-FLOOR)"; an arm emitting \(\Delta\hat z\equiv0\) makes the field cosine \(0/0\) and the magnitude ratio \(0/\lVert\Delta z\rVert\), is refused on those two columns and on no other, and is scored on the position-matched per-coordinate NRMSE vector and on the sign column's McNemar, where both are well defined (\(\lVert\Delta\hat z-\Delta z\rVert\) needs no direction; the sign of \(0\) is a registered tie under the McNemar's discordant-pair rule). The consequence row's floor cell is corrected to read "exact oracle \(0.0\); the no-change predictor's error printed on the position-matched NRMSE column only, which is the column it is scored on", and the Statement states that this NRMSE is the number the floor cell prints. Every refused cell journals refused_columns = [cosine, magnitude_ratio], and 04.15's field list gains refused_columns — "the per-column refusal scope of 04.8, empty list where nothing is refused, so a refusal is never a whole-cell absence" — so the scope is auditable under 04.15's own refusal rule. The magnitude ratio is added to the refused set beyond what the required repair names, because it is \(0/\lVert\Delta z\rVert\) on the same arm and refusing only the cosine would leave a second undefined column scored. Limits records the per-column reading once.

docs.title: A-49 · verse 04.10 · severity repair
docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). The \(\tau\) ladder is in NRMSE units, so T1 and T2 are undefined on two of the book's four heads and on one of its three beds, contradicting the Statement's scope. Mechanism (verbatim). V-17, D-1 Number (verbatim). Statement: "two numbers per bed and arm pair" with \(\tau\) from "\(\{0.9,0.8,0.7,0.5\}\) in NRMSE-to-oracle units". 04.8 scores the argmin head by accuracy with Clopper-Pearson and 04.7's capability channel by a Bernoulli sign rate; neither has an NRMSE-to-oracle. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Register a second ladder in distance-to-floor units for rate-valued heads (accuracy relative to \(\mathrm{floor}_{\rm zeroinfo}\), four levels frozen), or state that T1/T2 are defined on vector heads only and mark the argmin and chess channels NOT MEASURED — needs a rate-valued $\tau$ ladder. Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.10. Both halves of the required repair are taken, because the second alone would leave the chess bed with no ladder at all. The Statement's scope is corrected to "two numbers per bed, arm pair and head", and two ladders are registered. The vector-head ladder is the existing \(\{0.9,0.8,0.7,0.5\}\) in NRMSE-to-oracle units and is now scoped explicitly to the three vector heads of 04.8 — \(q\), \(z^\star\), \(\Delta z\) — each of which is scored by a position-matched NRMSE against an exact oracle at \(0.0\) and anchored at \(1.0\) for the mean predictor (04.3), with the statement printed that it covers no rate-valued head and that a \(\tau\) read off it on one is a threshold imported out of its units (V-17). The rate-head ladder is registered here as this book's second ladder, in distance-to-floor units, \(\tau_{\rm rate}=(1-\mathrm{acc})/\mathrm{floor}\) with four levels frozen at the same four numbers (M-2), the floor being \(\mathrm{floor}_{\rm zeroinfo}=1-\max_a\hat\pi(a^\star)\) on 04.8's argmin head (04.3's own second floor object) and \(\mathrm{base}_k(h{=}8)=\max\{p_k,1-p_k\}\) on 04.7's eval-\(\Delta\) capability channel (04.7's own fourth floor object); \(\tau_{\rm rate}\) reads \(1\) at chance and \(0\) at the exact oracle, which is the vector ladder's anchoring, so the two carry the same four levels without either being read in the other's units, and the floor is recomputed on the batch being scored. The ladder id is printed in the cell. T1 and T2 on the argmin head and on the chess capability channel now read NOT MEASURED against a defined denominator — needs $\mathrm{floor}_{\rm zeroinfo}$ from the first admitted batch (04.21 step 5) and needs $\mathrm{base}_k(8)$ from one rollout pass over the $36$ fixture games (04.7) — where before they read against no unit at all. The Kill gains a clause: a T1 or T2 on a rate-valued head read against the NRMSE ladder, or on a vector head read against the rate ladder, is struck as V-17, decided at \(0\) GPU-s by the ladder id against 04.8's head table; the "no level reached" clause now reads "no level of the head's own registered ladder", as does link 1's kill. The Evidence prints both ladders' units, both denominators with their NOT MEASURED markers, and the statement that the four levels are this book's frozen constants and are not fitted to any result. Limits records the two ladders once, naming the two heads and the one bed that had no ladder before.

docs.text:
Flaw (verbatim). "Absent from the output" is not "reads 0", so the two-way calibration validates only the positive half. Mechanism (verbatim). V-7, V-14 Number (verbatim). A grep -rho '"kind": *"[a-z_0-9]*"' | uniq -c census cannot distinguish a kind emitted zero times from a kind that was never spelled that way or that is emitted outside results/**/*.jsonl. arm_phase 0 is inferred from absence. replacement_survives (verbatim). true Required repair (verbatim). Severity (verbatim). repair

Repair applied — 04.14. The enumeration is run and both sets are printed. RUN this session, grep -rhoE '^NAME = "[a-zA-Z_0-9]+"' ceq scale scripts --include='*.py' returns \(13\) declared arm names (arm_a_k1, arm_phase, arm_pl, arm_smprime, ceq, ceq_hybrid, chase_eprocess, chase_m3_synth, m2, m3_quintuple_v2, r2, s2, wilson_arms), each emitted as "kind": NAME; RUN this session, grep -rhoE '"kind" *: *"[a-zA-Z_0-9]+"' ceq scale scripts --include='*.py' | sort -u returns \(20\) literal kinds; the two sets are disjoint, so \(33\) kinds are declared emitters. The Hypotheses therefore state the counter's reach as measured on the lower side and unmeasured on the upper, and the Kill's second clause is restated: as written ("the census reads above \(0\) for a kind no script emits") it fires today on all nine and is a kill satisfied by construction against its own counter (V-10); it now reads "a kind above \(0\) reachable from no emit site under the extended enumeration" and is registered unreachable, NOT MEASURED — needs the emit-site enumeration extended past literal spellings, with the note that no verse reads it as having fired. docs.title: 05 — REPAIRS: every break as a plan with a price and a verification number
docs.text:
MERCURY · LESTRADE — pricing, scheduling, execution. This book does not interpret; it prices, orders and verifies. Written 2026-09-05 under docs/canon/CHARTER.md at HEAD 99777ab.

Preface — what this book decides, and the verse that decides it first. The book decides the order in which the broken things are repaired, the price of each repair in GPU-seconds and evenings, and the single number that shows each repair worked. The first decision is verse 05.2: the box that decides every research number no longer runs the stack it was certified on — torch 2.14.0+cpu and numpy 2.4.6 were installed over the certified torch 2.5.1+cu121 / numpy 1.26.4, CUDA is not visible to the installed torch, and pytest -q at the root collects 2,580 tests and runs 0 behind 22 collection errors (RUN 2026-09-06). Until 05.3 lands, no number in any book can be RUN on the certified device, so 05.3 is evening 1 and nothing is scheduled before it. The book then prices, in order: the device re-certification split into a ≤20 GPU-s half and a 523.9 s half (05.5); the three harness debts of scripts/v15_r1.py with the test that proves each (05.6–05.8); the prose-coupled test policy and the registry the deletion severed (05.9); the Gate-0 circularity as a written rule (05.10); the five open rulings with the default each takes (05.11); the package, the residual and the unpinned sources (05.12); the documentation discipline with its census command (05.13); the first five evenings and the critical path (05.14); and a scheduling row for every census item another book closes (05.15).

Price basis, stated once. GPU-seconds are quoted from the record's own unit prices on the certified RTX 4060 Laptop at ab5b485: one 150-step control cell \(1.524\) s [FITTED], one shape cell on the softmax corner \(1.681\) s [FITTED + RUN], the capped cell \(1.884\) s, fixed cost per invocation \(4.0\) s (READ docs/PLAN.md:971-978 @ 99777ab); one ragged LM step at the Q3 shape \(0.299025\) s [MEASURED] (READ COSTS.md:212,239 @ 99777ab); the full device certificate \(523.9\) s [MEASURED] (READ COSTS.md:62 @ 99777ab). Every one of these is a per-op floor under a \(2.0\times\)–\(6.6\times\) dispatch gap (READ scale/m3_flops.py:101-121 @ 99777ab) and a laptop clock that is not stationary at \(\pm12\) per cent (READ docs/PLAN.md:967 @ 99777ab); prices are therefore "at least" until 05.5 re-measures them on the re-certified stack. An evening is one sitting; the first five evenings are each capped at \(20\) GPU-s by the budget declared in 05.1 — [ASSUMED], with its reason printed there. The CHARTER carries no such cap: RUN grep -c "20 GPU" docs/canon/CHARTER.md reads \(0\), and the book-05 scope row is docs/canon/CHARTER.md:269 (live), which names "the price in evenings and GPU-s" and no number.

docs.title: 05.1 — The ordering rule: cheapest-decisive-first, with the evening cap
docs.text:
Statement. Repairs are ordered by the pair (price of the kill, decisiveness of the kill), cheapest first, and ties are broken toward the repair whose kill withdraws more of the canon if it fires. A repair whose kill cannot fire on the tree as it stands is not scheduled (reachability rule). The order is: environment (05.2–05.4) → certificate (05.5) → harness (05.6–05.8) → tests (05.9) → gate rule (05.10) → rulings (05.11) → package and sources (05.12) → documentation census (05.13). Every evening among the first five costs at most \(20\) GPU-s; the first evening above the cap is the full certificate rerun at \(523.9\) s, and it is evening 6.

The cap, declared here because nothing else declares it. \(20.0\) GPU-s per evening among the first five is an [ASSUMED] budget of this book, not an inherited threshold. Its reason: the largest single repair price among the first five is 05.7's interleaved 8 cells at \(17.63\) s DERIVED, and \(20.0\) leaves one invocation's fixed cost (\(4.0\) s, READ docs/PLAN.md:978 @ 99777ab) of headroom above it without admitting a second 8-cell run — so the cap is the smallest round number that admits every priced repair singly and refuses every pair of them. It is not read from the CHARTER: RUN git ls-tree -r 99777ab --name-only | grep -ci canon reads \(0\) (the canon is untracked at the pin, git status reads ?? docs/canon/), and RUN grep -c "20 GPU" docs/canon/CHARTER.md on the live file reads \(0\). Every docs/canon/ citation in this book is therefore to the live file with no @ 99777ab pin, and the canon's own pin is its birth commit, which does not exist yet.

Hypotheses. The certified device is the RTX 4060 Laptop, \(7.996\) GiB, sm_8.9 (READ COSTS.md:56-58 @ 99777ab); the driver on the box reads 595.79 with CUDA Version: 13.2 (RUN nvidia-smi, 2026-09-05), which serves a cu121 wheel by the driver's backward compatibility ([ASSUMED] — the toolkit compatibility rule is vendor documentation, not measured here; 05.3's verification command is what measures it). No Kaggle number enters any price (V-22).

Evidence. Unit prices: READ docs/PLAN.md:971-978 @ 99777ab; READ COSTS.md:62,212 @ 99777ab. The dispatch gap: READ scale/m3_flops.py:101-121 @ 99777ab. The cap of \(20\) GPU-s: [ASSUMED], declared above with its reason; the book-05 scope row it is not taken from is READ docs/canon/CHARTER.md:269 (live, no pin — RUN git ls-tree -r 99777ab --name-only | grep -ci canon reads \(0\)).

Mechanism. M-8 (pricing every arm at one arm's rate — each price below names its arm); P-8 (an upper bound stated as a price — every price carries "at least"); D-6 (a repair written and never started — every repair here has an evening number and a verification command).

Kill. Any verse of this book whose evening lies among the first five and whose priced GPU-seconds exceed \(20\) at the quoted unit prices. Frozen threshold: \(20.0\) GPU-s. Instrument: the arithmetic printed in each verse's Kill line. Price: \(0\). Planted negative: the full certificate at \(523.9\) s, which the rule must refuse from the first five — and does (it is evening 6).

The rule fired on this book's own first draft, and the split is applied here. 05.6's kill needs an identical-seed pair at --device cuda --seeds 0 --arms softmax and a third run at --s 32 --arms arm_pl (a gated arm, because the bind row the --s clause reads is emitted only for GATED_ARMS = ("arm_pl", "arm_smprime"), RUN grep -n "GATED_ARMS *=" scripts/v15_r1.py reads :146), priced \(2\times(1.524+4.0)+(1.884+4.0)=16.93\) s — \(11.05\) [FITTED] plus a \(5.88\) s [ASSUMED] ceiling, because both unit prices are defined at \(s=64\) and the third run is at \(s=32\) (05.6's price paragraph, and its kill clause (v) audits the ceiling on the same run); 05.7's needs 8 interleaved cells over arms \(\{\)arm_pl, softmax\(\}\) and seeds \(0\)–\(3\), priced \(4\times1.884+4\times1.524+4.0=17.63\) s. The two need different --arms and different --seeds, so they cannot share an invocation, and a single evening 3 would cost \(16.93+17.63=34.56\) GPU-s — above the frozen \(20.0\). Under this verse's own If-killed the evening is split, most-decisive first: evening 3 is 05.7's 8 interleaved cells (\(17.63\) s, the timer is the instrument every later price depends on), evening 3b is 05.6's pair plus the --s 32 run (\(16.93\) s), and evening 3c is 05.8's one arm_smprime cell (\(1.884+4.0=5.88\) s) — 3b and 3c cannot be merged (\(16.93+5.88=22.81\) s, above the cap). 05.14 carries the three sittings and their sum. The phrase "05.6's pair is inside the same invocation set" is deleted from 05.14: it named a shared invocation that the differing --arms and --seeds make impossible.

If killed. The offending verse's evening is split: the ≤20 GPU-s sub-run first (the one that decides the most), the remainder pushed to evening 6 or later. Hypotheses: the verse's kill is decidable on the sub-run alone. Evidence: the verse's own price arithmetic. Kill of the replacement: the sub-run does not decide the verse's kill (its kill number is not produced by the sub-run) — then the verse leaves the first five entirely and the critical path in 05.14 lengthens by one evening.

Terminal. The order stands as a list even if every price is wrong: the canon licenses "repair in this order" and withdraws every GPU-second figure until 05.5 re-measures them.

The drift is dated, and the dating evidence is [ASSUMED], because an mtime is a filesystem write and not a producer record. The torch, functorch, numpy and numpy-2.4.6.dist-info directories in site-packages carry mtime 2026-09-03 23:30–23:31 (RUN ls --time-style=long-iso), three days after the certificate of 2026-08-31 22:26. That reading is tagged [ASSUMED] — mtime is a filesystem write, not a producer record, and this tree proves why in its own results/: RUN over results/, \(331\) files carry \(176\) distinct mtimes, and the \(18\) files 05.2's Terminal names share the single minute 2026-09-04 00:41 across only four sub-millisecond stamps (\(1788462678.5325522\), \(\ldots5385008\) on eleven files, \(\ldots5439267\) on two, \(\ldots5445810\) on four) — eighteen files, four write instants, one bulk handling event. A stamp that records eighteen files as four writes cannot be read as eighteen measurements, and the same objection applies to a package directory.

The dated half of the drift is carried on the install record instead, which pip writes once at install and never touches again: numpy-2.4.6.dist-info/ holds INSTALLER, RECORD, WHEEL, METADATA, DELVEWHEEL and entry_points.txt, all at 2026-09-03 23:30 (RUN ls --time-style=long-iso -l). Its undated half is stronger still and needs no clock at all: the directory's name is numpy-2.4.6.dist-info and there is no numpy-1.26.4.dist-info beside it, so the interpreter that answers import numpy is carrying a distribution the certificate never named — a fact about which files exist, not about when. The canon reads the drift off the name and quotes the date [ASSUMED].

Hypotheses. The interpreter is <home>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python311\python.exe — a machine-wide CPython 3.11 install, not a repo-local venv — (RUN); the root suite is collected with pytest.ini's norecursedirs excluding attic and kaggle (READ pytest.ini:19 @ 99777ab); the counts are of files, not of tests.

Evidence.
